tracks.title: Thirty-Three In The Queue
tracks.mood: too old for it and glad to be there
tracks.subject: queueing for a club where everyone else is twenty
tracks.caption: UK garage in the two-step style. Shuffled two-step drum pattern with skipped kicks and swung sixteenth hi-hats, short organ chord stabs on the offbeats, a wobbling sub bass, pitched-up and chopped R&B vocal samples answering the lead, a filtered string pad on the chorus. Swung and skippy with a heavy sub and a crisp bright top, mixed for a club system. Male voice, conversational in the verses with a light melodic lift on the hook, no autotune. 132 BPM, F minor. Too old for it and glad to be there. No four-on-the-floor house kick, no trap hi-hat rolls, no rap verse, no acoustic instruments, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - two-step drums and organ stab]

[Verse 1]
Queue goes round the corner and everybody's twenty
I'm thirty-three in a jacket I bought for a wedding
Bouncer looks at my ID longer than he looks at theirs
Then he laughs, and he lets me in, and he says "big man"

[Pre-Chorus]
I came here for one song
I don't even know if they still play it

[Chorus]
Thirty-three in the queue
And the bass still finds my ribs the same way it used to
Nobody in here knows what I do on a Monday
For two hours I'm not anybody's anything

[Verse 2]
Girl next to me asks if I'm somebody's dad
I say no, I'm somebody's ex and somebody's tenant
She laughs and hands me her water without asking
That's the most looked-after I have felt all year

[Chorus]
Thirty-three in the queue
And the bass still finds my ribs the same way it used to
Nobody in here knows what I do on a Monday
For two hours I'm not anybody's anything, and they played it

[Outro - vocal chop and sub]
Taxi? No. I'm walking.
Forty minutes. I'll feel it Tuesday.

tracks.title: Dad On The Decks
tracks.mood: meeting your father before he was your father
tracks.subject: a sixty-one-year-old father pulling a sheet off two turntables in the loft
tracks.caption: Jungle in the current revival style. Chopped and time-stretched Amen and Think breakbeats running fast and rearranged every few bars, deep 808 sub drops on the downbeats, a warm sustained soul pad, a short ragga vocal sample used as punctuation, a reese bass entering in the second half. Fast busy breaks under a slow warm vocal, with a very heavy sub and the breaks slightly crunchy. Female voice singing smoothly at half-time over the breaks, soulful and unhurried. 172 BPM, A minor. Meeting your father before he became your father. No four-on-the-floor, no trap drums, no autotune, no acoustic guitar, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - chopped break and sub drop]

[Verse 1]
Loft above the garage, two turntables under a sheet
Dad says "I used to do this" and I said "sure you did"
He pulled the sheet off. Wiped them with his sleeve.
Put a record on and his whole spine changed

[Chorus]
Dad on the decks
Sixty-one years old and his hands know something I don't
He's not my dad for these ten minutes
He's a kid in ninety-four who hasn't met my mum yet

[Verse 2]
He shows me how to catch the break right on the one
I miss it four times, he doesn't say anything
Fifth time I get it and he doesn't say anything either
He just turns the bass up. That's how he says it.

[Chorus]
Dad on the decks
Sixty-one years old and his hands know something I don't
He's not my dad for these ten minutes
He's a kid in ninety-four, and now I've met him

[Outro - break stops, needle lift]
Sheet's back on
He left the plug in

tracks.title: Mr Kim Calls Me Professor
tracks.mood: a nickname that turned out to be a prophecy
tracks.subject: a corner store owner who nicknamed a twelve-year-old Professor
tracks.caption: Baltimore club rap. The classic Baltimore club kick pattern with its syncopated boom-boom-bap feel, a looped Think break underneath, short shouted chant samples answering the rapper, layered hand claps, a simple stabbed synth bass. Raw and loud with the kicks forward and almost no reverb, deliberately rough rather than polished. Male rap voice with his cadence locked tightly to the eighth-note grid, conversational and proud, with call-and-response chants on the hook. 130 BPM, G minor. A nickname that turned out to be a prophecy. No trap hi-hat rolls, no Jersey club bed squeak, no sung pop chorus, no autotune, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - Baltimore club kicks and Think break]

[Verse 1]
Corner store on Greenmount, Mr Kim behind the glass
Calls everybody something, never once your name
Big Man, Sneakers, Little Sister, Doctor, Boss
Me he calls Professor 'cause I read the cereal box

[Hook]
Mr Kim calls me Professor
Twelve years old, I didn't earn it, now I'm thirty and I'm trying
Every time I walk in he says it like it's true
And I stand up straighter every single time

[Verse 2]
Told him last week I finally finished the degree
Night school, six years, nobody threw me a thing
He came round the counter, which he never does
Shook my hand and gave me a soda and wouldn't let me pay

[Hook]
Mr Kim calls me Professor
Twelve years old, I didn't earn it, now I'm thirty and I earned it
Every time I walk in he says it like it's true
And now it is, and he was first

[Outro - chant and kicks]
Professor. Professor.
Green soda. On the house.

tracks.title: Unexpected Item
tracks.mood: being a function until somebody sees a person
tracks.subject: the one human attendant for six self-checkout machines
tracks.caption: London new-generation underground rap. A detuned glitchy synth melody that stutters and repitches, jerk- and garage-inflected drums played at double-time, a cloudy smeared bass, occasional scanner-beep sound effects used as rhythm. Cloudy and glitchy with the whole mix slightly smeared and soft, no hard trap gloss. Male rap voice in a London accent, mumbled and melodic, low in the mix and half-sung, no heavy autotune. 150 BPM, D minor. Being treated as a function until one person sees a man. No 808 trap drums, no American cadence, no big sung chorus, no live instruments, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - glitchy synth and jerk drums]

[Verse 1]
Six self-checkouts and one of me
I'm the human the machine calls when it can't cope
Unexpected item in the bagging area, all day
That's my name on this shift, that's my whole job title

[Hook]
Unexpected item
That's what they call me when the system gets confused
Fourteen times an hour I walk over and fix it
Nobody looks up, I'm a function, not a man

[Verse 2]
Old lady's bananas won't scan, she's apologising
To the machine, not me, she's saying sorry to the screen
I tap my card, I say "you're alright", she looks at me
Surprised there was a person under all the beeping

[Hook]
Unexpected item
That's what they call me when the system gets confused
Fourteen times an hour I walk over and fix it
And once today somebody saw a man

[Outro - synth stutters out]
Approval needed
Approved

tracks.title: They Put A Rowing Machine Where My Bed Was
tracks.mood: happy for her and lost at the same time
tracks.subject: coming home to find your childhood bedroom turned into your mother's home gym
tracks.caption: Midwest emo in the twinkle style. Two clean electric guitars in an open alternate tuning playing interlocking tapped arpeggios, splashy drums with lots of crash and ride, a melodic bass moving under the guitars, bars that shift meter between sections, a trumpet line in the bridge. Bright and intricate with big dynamic swings between quiet tapped passages and loud full-band sections. Male voice, earnest and strained, half-shouted in the choruses and cracking on purpose. 140 BPM with shifting meters, F major. Happy for her and lost at the same time. No distortion wall, no synth, no autotune, no programmed drums, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - tapped clean guitars]

[Verse 1]
Came home for Christmas, opened my old door
Mum's turned it into a gym, there's a rowing machine
Exactly where my bed was, the dent's still in the carpet
She's very proud of it. She rows at six a.m.

[Pre-Chorus]
I said "that's great, Mum" and I meant it
I also sat on the rowing machine for an hour

[Chorus]
They put a rowing machine where my bed was
And I'm happy for her, I swear I'm happy for her
It's just strange to find out you were a room
And the room moved on before you did

[Verse 2]
The glow stars are still up on the ceiling
She couldn't reach them, so they stayed
I lay on the floor where the bed used to be
Fourteen stars, I counted, same as when I was eight

[Chorus]
They put a rowing machine where my bed was
And I'm happy for her, I swear I'm happy for her
It's just strange to find out you were a room
And the room moved on, and kept the stars for me

[Outro - guitars cut]
I rowed two thousand metres
Terrible time. She beat it.
[Song ends abruptly]

tracks.title: Bakar Ikan
tracks.mood: a family with only one question
tracks.subject: grilling skipjack on an Ambon beach with every cousin who came home
tracks.caption: Eastern Indonesian party pop in the Lagu Timur style. A rubbery, bouncy synth bass carrying a syncopated tropical groove, light Latin-leaning percussion with shakers and congas, a clean electric guitar picking short melodic hooks, hand claps on the chorus, no kendang and no suling. Warm, swinging and light, built for dancing rather than loudness. Relaxed male voice singing in Ambon Malay dialect with light autotune, answered by a group in call-and-response on the chorus. 98 BPM, A major. A family that asks only one question. No dangdut koplo rhythm, no kendang, no trap drums, no ballad section, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - synth bass and tropical percussion]

[Verse 1]
Sore di pantai Ambon, sepupu semua datang
Ikan cakalang di atas bara, sambal colo-colo dalam toples
Om Yopi pegang kipas, dia bilang "jang ganggu"
Dari kecil dia yang bakar, sampai sekarang dia yang bakar

[Chorus - call and response]
Bakar ikan, bakar ikan, dong samua datang
Seng ada yang tanya kerja apa, seng ada yang tanya kapan kawin
Cuma satu yang ditanya: "su makan?"
Kalau balom, dudu, ambil piring

[Verse 2]
Sepupu dari Jakarta su lupa logat
Dua jam di sini, logatnya pulang sendiri
Kami tertawa, dia tertawa paling keras
Dia bilang dia rindu, dia bilang itu waktu matahari su turun

[Chorus - call and response]
Bakar ikan, bakar ikan, dong samua datang
Seng ada yang tanya kerja apa, seng ada yang tanya kapan kawin
Cuma satu yang ditanya: "su makan?"
Kalau balom, dudu, ambil piring, ambil dua

[Outro - percussion fades]
Matahari turun
Om Yopi masih bakar

tracks.title: Marga
tracks.mood: instant family in a city of strangers
tracks.subject: finding your own clan name on a stranger's business card in Jakarta
tracks.caption: Batak pop in the classic trio style. Three male voices singing in close three-part harmony carrying almost the entire song, sulim bamboo flute playing the melodic introductions and answers, taganing tuned drums keeping a soft pattern, a steel-string acoustic guitar strumming gently underneath. Warm and close with the three voices forward and the instruments sparse and supportive. Male trio in tight, resonant three-part harmony, the lead taking the verses alone and the other two joining on every chorus. 78 BPM, G major. Instant family in a city full of strangers. No drum kit, no synth, no autotune, no rap, no key change.

tracks.title: Pohon Beringin
tracks.mood: a village that will not lift the axe
tracks.subject: the old banyan at the edge of the village standing on the red line of a road map
tracks.caption: Indonesian experimental music on self-built bamboo string instruments. Bamboo string instruments bowed and plucked with rough, unrefined attack, scraping and resonating, a sustained low bamboo drone, occasional percussive strikes on the bamboo body, no drum kit and no conventional harmony. Raw and confrontational, unquantised and free-flowing, recorded close so every scrape and breath is present. Male voice moving between plain speech, ritual chant and harsh throat-overtone singing, intense rather than soothing. Around 66 BPM with a loose free pulse, D minor. A village that will not be the one to lift the axe. No drum kit, no synth, no pop structure polish, no autotune, no key change.

tracks.title: Merantau
tracks.genre: pop Minang with saluang and talempong
tracks.mood: the custom that never says how to wave
tracks.subject: a son leaving Bukittinggi to merantau and his father checking the motorbike tyres three times
tracks.caption: Minangkabau pop. Saluang end-blown bamboo flute carrying the lead melody with its breathy circular-breathing tone, talempong small gong-chimes playing interlocking figures, rabab fiddle answering the voice, a soft frame drum keeping the pulse, a steel-string acoustic guitar strumming quietly underneath. Airy and melancholic with the saluang's breath fully audible and plenty of space. Male voice with Minang vocal ornament on held notes, warm and restrained. 88 BPM, E minor. The custom that never tells you how to wave goodbye. No drum kit, no synth, no DJ remix beat, no autotune, no key change.

tracks.subject: a son standing where his father called fish auctions for fifty years
tracks.caption: Japanese minyo funk played by a live band. tracks.caption: Thai classical piphat ensemble cut against club production. tracks.title: นาหลังเกี่ยว
tracks.mood: learning to see next year
tracks.subject: sitting on the paddy dyke beside your father for an hour after harvest
tracks.caption: Thai khaen music reworked as dub techno. Khaen mouth organ drones and short riffs fed through tape delay so every phrase repeats and decays, dub techno chord stabs filtered and echoing into the distance, a deep soft four-on-the-floor kick, a rolling sub bass, slow hi-hats evolving over minutes. Deep, dubby and cavernous with long echo tails and slow change rather than drops. Male voice, low and sparse, each line echoed back by the delay. 118 BPM, D minor. Learning to see next year. No luk thung arrangement, no trap drums, no autotune, no guitar, no key change.

tracks.mood: a street that only notices its song when it stops
tracks.subject: a papaya salad vendor who sings molam while pounding, and the evening she doesn't
tracks.caption: Thai molam singing set over a jazz band. Drum kit played with brushes in a soft swing, upright bass walking, Rhodes electric piano playing jazz seventh chords, khaen mouth organ answering the voice in the gaps. Intimate jazz-club sound with the brushes and Rhodes warm and the voice forward. Female voice singing with full Isan molam ornamentation, trills and long held notes, laid over the swing feel rather than adapting to it. 92 BPM, F minor. tracks.title: โทรศัพท์บ้าน
tracks.mood: the one thing a fading memory still keeps
tracks.subject: a cream-coloured landline a mother still pays for because a father in care calls it every Sunday
tracks.caption: Thai shoegaze with screamo dynamics. A dense wall of fuzzed guitars swelling and collapsing, slow heavy drums with crashing cymbals, a bass buried in the guitars, feedback bleeding between sections. Texture-first, with extreme contrast between near-silent whispered passages and walls of noise. Female voice whispering the verses very close to the microphone and screaming the chorus raw and hoarse. 118 BPM, B minor. The one thing a fading memory still keeps. No clean pop chorus, no synth, no autotune, no programmed drums, no key change.

tracks.title: lên núi thăm em
tracks.mood: someone needing only to be seen
tracks.subject: a four-hour bus ride to visit a younger sister teaching twelve children at a mountain school
tracks.caption: Vietnamese hat then tradition fused with rap. Dan tinh long-necked gourd lute plucked dry and forward carrying the melody, xoc nhac bell rattle shaken in the then rhythm, soft hip-hop drums with a gentle kick and rimshot, a light sub bass underneath. Earthy and dry with the lute forward and only a light modern low end. A soft, flowing then-style sung vocal with traditional ornament carrying the verses and chorus, alternating with a conversational male rap verse. 90 BPM, G pentatonic. Someone who needs only to be seen. No trap hi-hat rolls, no autotune, no EDM drop, no Western guitar, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - dan tinh and xoc nhac]

[Verse 1]
Bốn tiếng xe khách, hai tiếng xe ôm, ba mươi phút đi bộ
Em tôi dạy ở điểm trường trên núi, mười hai đứa học trò
Lớp học vách gỗ, bảng đen dựng vào tường
Em đứng đó, nhỏ hơn tôi nhớ, nhưng giọng em to hơn

[Verse 2 - Rap]
Tôi ngồi cuối lớp, mười hai cái đầu quay lại nhìn
Em nói "đây là anh cô", tụi nhỏ đồng thanh "chào anh"
Em dạy chữ, tụi nhỏ dạy em tiếng của tụi nó
Một buổi học, hai thứ tiếng, chẳng ai thiệt

[Chorus]
Lên núi thăm em
Em không cần tôi đưa xuống
Em chỉ cần có người thấy
Em đang làm gì ở trên này

[Verse 3 - Rap]
Tối đó em nấu cơm bằng bếp củi, khói cay mắt
Em nói tháng này lương về trễ, em cười
Tôi định đưa tiền, em đẩy lại, "anh mua sách cho tụi nhỏ đi"
Tôi mua hai mươi cuốn, tôi không nói em biết

[Chorus]
Lên núi thăm em
Em không cần tôi đưa xuống
Em chỉ cần có người thấy
Và hôm nay, người đó là tôi

[Outro - dan tinh alone]
Hai mươi cuốn sách
Em sẽ biết, khi tụi nhỏ đọc

tracks.title: 他說過的那片草
tracks.mood: fifty years folded into one word
tracks.subject: taking a herder's son back to the grassland he left fifty years ago
tracks.caption: Mandarin folk rock built on Mongolian instrumentation and the galloping horse rhythm. Morin khuur horsehead fiddle carrying the lead melody with its rough bowed tone and slides, tovshuur lute strumming the gallop pattern, drums playing a driving 6/8 horse-gallop figure on toms and kick, distorted rhythm guitar doubling the root underneath, a low throat-sung drone hum entering in the final chorus. Wide and open with the fiddle forward and the gallop driving everything. Male voice, weathered and low, singing plainly with a drone-like hum beneath the chorus. 116 BPM in a 6/8 gallop, D minor pentatonic. Fifty years folded into one word. No erhu, no guzheng, no synth pad, no trap drums, no key change.
